items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: He said, 'we want you to join the band starting October 8.' ... I was 24 years old and no rehearsal. My rehearsal was in the dressing room with Basie saying, 'Is there anything I should know here? I’m only 24 years old why did I get this gig.'

ctx.x: You’re diving into the whole thing.

Yeah. You know, drinking and smoking pot and girls and all that stuff, and I was just happy going to band and playing gigs along the way. And I said hey, this isn’t terrible. Forget those classes. So eventually technically I flunked out of Eastern Michigan. So I laid off a semester and went back on my own dime, I went and found a day job, along with doing the other gigs, and got my own apartment, and went back as a music major, a music education major, taking clarinet and theory and all that stuff. And I got a…
would get that job and stay in school and just do that. And about three months after I did that I got a phone call. It was Labor Day 1982 and it was Count Basie calling me personally.

items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: So I get the call from Count Basie... we want you to join the band starting October 8.

ctx.x: I think he called himself Bill.

Yeah the guys called him a various assortment of names. Bill, Chief. I called him Chief. Some guys called him Count. Other guys called him Boss. It didn’t matter, he was just so well respected. He was a great guy. So I get the call from Count Basie. So he said, “Sonny Cohn, the manager, will be calling you shortly and he’ll let you know all the details.” He said, “we want you to join the band starting October 8.” And that was Labor Day. So that’s like six weeks. I was registered for school, all ready to go back…
